package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all versions using compromised shared JS libraries)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript skimming script is designed to steal credit card information from users of over 200 online university campus stores by intercepting payment data entered into checkout forms and exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a Magecart-style web skimming attack that compromises the integrity of the e-commerce platform and results in large-scale payment card data theft.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user submits the payment form
execution_context.file_location: Shared JavaScript library loaded by PrismWeb commerce platform (e.g., /js/shared.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits the payment form, the code attaches an event listener to the payment form's submit event, reads credit card data from input fields, and exfiltrates this data to an attacker-controlled domain via an HTTP request, resulting in theft of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script intercepts sensitive payment data directly from the DOM and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is a clear indicator of web skimming activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should never transmit payment data to third-party or untrusted domains; payment data should only be sent securely to authorized payment processors via backend channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may access payment form fields for client-side validation or formatting, but they do not transmit raw payment data to external destinations.
key_indicators: Event listener attached to payment form submission
Direct collection of credit card fields (number, expiry, CVV) from DOM
Outbound network request to an untrusted, non-payment-processor domain (e.g., attacker.com/collect)
Use of obfuscation or encoding (e.g., btoa) to hide exfiltrated data

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the PrismWeb shared JavaScript library and injects the skimming code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded by all online stores using the compromised shared library.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript executes in the browser when a user visits a compromised store and fills out the payment form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credit card data is intercepted at the point of form submission.

attack_chain.action: Stolen payment data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure via an HTTP request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker collects and monetizes stolen credit card information.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript event listeners on payment forms that transmit form data to external or untrusted domains
Unexpected network requests containing payment data (credit card number, expiry, CVV) at the moment of form submission
Presence of obfuscated or injected code blocks in shared JavaScript libraries, especially those loaded on payment pages
file_indicators: Modifications to shared JavaScript files (e.g., /js/shared.js) that are not present in official releases or version control
Presence of new, suspicious, or obfuscated code blocks in e-commerce platform scripts, particularly those loaded on checkout pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor (e.g., attacker.com/collect)
Unusual traffic from payment pages to external domains, especially at the time of form submission
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes in shared JavaScript libraries, especially those loaded by payment or checkout pages. Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict data exfiltration to untrusted domains. Analyze network traffic from payment pages for unexpected destinations or payloads containing payment data. Scan for event listeners on payment forms that transmit data externally. Employ file integrity monitoring and version control checks on e-commerce platform scripts to detect unauthorized modifications.
